elements.name: Page Object
elements.what: A test-side object that wraps a UI page or fragment behind an application-specific API, so tests manipulate intention-revealing methods instead of raw HTML/widget structure.
elements.problem: UI-driving tests coupled directly to page structure break en masse on every markup change; a page object centralizes the UI knowledge in one place and keeps test logic readable and stable.
elements.named_in: Fowler, bliki 'PageObject' (10 Sep 2013; loaded live — states it was first described as Window Driver at eaaDev and popularized as 'page object' by Selenium); Selenium project documentation

elements.name: Tolerant Reader
elements.what: A consumer-side reading strategy that extracts only the data elements it needs from a payload, ignores unknown or extra content, and makes minimal assumptions about structure.
elements.problem: Strictly schema-bound consumers break whenever a service provider evolves its message format; reading tolerantly (Postel's robustness principle applied to payload consumption) lets providers add or rearrange elements without breaking existing clients.
elements.named_in: Fowler, bliki 'TolerantReader' (9 May 2011; loaded live — notes Rob Daigneau published the full pattern in Service Design Patterns, Addison-Wesley 2011)

elements.name: Memory Image
elements.what: Keep the authoritative application state entirely in main memory and obtain durability by logging every state-changing event to persistent storage, replaying the log (accelerated by periodic snapshots) to rebuild state after restart.
elements.problem: Routing all state through a database costs IO and mapping complexity; when the working set fits in RAM, an event log plus snapshots gives durability while the program works at memory speed with plain in-memory structures.
elements.named_in: Fowler, bliki 'MemoryImage' (31 Aug 2011; loaded live — cites Prevayler/'system prevalence' and the LMAX architecture as realizations)
tags: borderline: composes event-sourcing + checkpointing/snapshot and Fowler frames it as an architectural approach; included because it is a single-process persistence mechanism with library-level realizations (Prevayler) and its own established name (system prevalence)

elements.name: Rules Engine
elements.what: A component that evaluates a collection of independent condition-action (production) rules against working state, with the engine — not imperative code order — deciding which rules fire, including chaining when one rule's action changes another rule's condition.
elements.problem: Domain logic consisting of many independent, frequently-changing decision rules becomes tangled when hard-coded as nested conditionals; representing it as declarative rules run by an evaluation loop keeps each rule separate and independently modifiable.
elements.named_in: Fowler, bliki 'RulesEngine' (7 Jan 2009; loaded live — 'you can build a simple rules engine yourself', production rules, Rete, chaining); production rule system literature (Forgy, Rete algorithm, 1982)
tags: borderline: also a commercial product category (BRMS) at system scale; included at the in-process altitude Fowler describes (rule objects + evaluation loop inside one application), sibling of behavior-tree/interpreter

parked_architecture.name: Event Collaboration (Fowler, eaaDev 'Focusing on Events')
parked_architecture.why: Components coordinate by broadcasting events instead of making requests — as a cross-component interaction style this is event-driven architecture's territory (Phase 3); its in-process mechanisms are already cataloged (observer, event-aggregator, domain-event, message-queue).

parked_architecture.name: Reporting Database (Fowler, bliki 2004)
parked_architecture.why: Separate database fed from the operational store for reporting/analytics — system-level data topology, fails altitude upward.

parked_architecture.name: Bounded Context (Evans DDD; Fowler bliki 2014)
parked_architecture.why: Strategic-design decomposition of a large model/system into contexts with explicit boundaries — system-structure altitude, Phase 3 (belongs with the DDD strategic set alongside already-parked Service Layer etc.).

parked_architecture.name: Polyglot Persistence (Fowler/Sadalage, bliki 2011)
parked_architecture.why: Using different datastore technologies per data need across a system — data-architecture stance, Phase 3 territory.

excluded_notable.name: CQRS (verification, not a new decision)
excluded_notable.why: VERIFIED already parked: merged_design.json carries the poeaa-ddd scout's park ('splitting a system's read and write models is an architecture style, Fowler bliki 2011; Greg Young') plus the wiki-longtail duplicate. No action needed.

excluded_notable.name: Role Interface (Fowler bliki 2006)
excluded_notable.why: Interface-granularity vocabulary (interface shaped per collaborator role, contrasted with Header Interface); ISP-adjacent characterization of interface design, not a distinct implementable mechanism beyond 'an interface'. Catalog already carries the mechanism-bearing interface constructs (separated-interface, explicit-interface, extension-interface, marker-interface).

excluded_notable.name: Header Interface (Fowler bliki 2006)
excluded_notable.why: Counterpart vocabulary to Role Interface (one interface mirroring a whole class); same rejection — characterization, not mechanism.

excluded_notable.name: Published Interface (Fowler bliki)
excluded_notable.why: Public-vs-published distinction is API-evolution/management vocabulary (who may depend on it), not an implementable mechanism — practice/altitude fail sideways.

excluded_notable.name: Local DTO (Fowler bliki 2004)

excluded_notable.name: Seedwork (Fowler bliki, term from Michael Feathers)
excluded_notable.why: Copy-then-diverge code-reuse approach for small starter kits — development practice vocabulary, weak establishedness as an element; excluded.

excluded_notable.name: Anemic Domain Model (Fowler bliki 2003)

excluded_notable.name: Data Clump (Fowler, Refactoring)
excluded_notable.why: Code smell, not a mechanism; refactoring/practice territory.

excluded_notable.name: Clock Wrapper (Fowler bliki)
excluded_notable.why: Injectable abstraction over the ambient time source for testability — application of dependency-injection + test-double to one dependency (time); fold, optionally as aka ('fake/virtual clock') on test-double.

excluded_notable.name: Window Driver (Fowler eaaDev)

excluded_notable.name: Given When Then (Fowler bliki 2013)
excluded_notable.why: Test-description convention (BDD scenario format, kin of arrange-act-assert) — a writing style/practice, not an implementable construct.

excluded_notable.name: Legacy Seam / Seam (Feathers WELC 2004; Fowler bliki LegacySeam)
excluded_notable.why: Analytical concept naming *where* behavior can be substituted without editing source (object/link/preprocessing seams) — a testability property of code plus legacy-work practice, not a recurring implementable mechanism; strictness round excludes.

excluded_notable.name: Contract Test (Fowler bliki 2011)
excluded_notable.why: Testing strategy verifying a test double (or provider) matches the real contract (consumer-driven contracts, Pact) — cross-component testing practice rather than an in-program construct; excluded at strictness peak.

excluded_notable.name: In Memory Test Database (Fowler bliki)
excluded_notable.why: Test-environment substitution technique — practice, plus covered conceptually by test-double/service-stub territory.

excluded_notable.name: Command Query Separation / Tell Don't Ask / Uniform Access / Hollywood Principle (bliki)
excluded_notable.why: Principles/guidelines, not mechanisms (DI, the mechanism behind Hollywood Principle, is already cataloged).

excluded_notable.name: Branch By Abstraction (Fowler bliki 2014)
excluded_notable.why: Transitional technique for large-scale change on trunk (introduce abstraction, migrate implementations, remove scaffolding) — change-sequencing practice, not a runtime mechanism.

excluded_notable.name: Parallel Change / Expand-Contract (Fowler bliki 2014)
excluded_notable.why: Interface-migration sequencing technique (expand, migrate, contract) — practice altitude, same family as Branch by Abstraction.

excluded_notable.name: Canary Release / Blue-Green Deployment / Dark Launching / Keystone Interface (bliki)
excluded_notable.why: Release-engineering and deployment practices — pass-7/ops territory, not design elements (feature-flag, the enabling mechanism, is already cataloged).

notes: Strictness-peak audit of martinfowler.com bliki + eaaDev. Method: full 682-line index read first; live fetches of the bliki front page, the eaaDev catalog page, and the API-design / testing / event-architectures tag indexes; every proposed element verified against its live primary bliki page; prior-round decisions checked in merged_design.json before re-judging. Charter items confirmed already present: feature-flag, collection-pipeline, fluent-interface, event-aggregator, notification, specification, event-sourcing, optimistic-offline-lock, gateway, mapper, object-mother; audit additionally confirmed present-or-folded: audit-log, temporal-property (temporal object/effectivity/snapshot as aka), domain-event, range, data-binding, humble-object, test-double, money, value-object, function-control (flag argument). CQRS park verified. Yield: 4 new elements (page-object certain; tolerant-reader certain, book-cataloged by Daigneau; memory-image and rules-engine borderline-tagged) — near the top of the expected 0-5 band but each is live-verified, book-or-bliki established, and genuinely absent under all names/akas. 4 new architecture parks (Event Collaboration, Reporting Database, Bounded Context, Polyglot Persistence). ~28 recorded rejections constitute the saturation evidence: the Fowler corpus beyond these is principles, practices, smells, frozen drafts, and vocabulary. Side observation for the editor (out of my charter): Meszaros xUnit fixture vocabulary (test fixture / fresh vs shared fixture / four-phase test) has no dedicated entry in testing-constructs; a targeted judge-call there may be warranted before Phase 1 closes.
